newsitem.title: INDIA: Court allows liquor, army at Miss World pageant.
newsitem.headline: Court allows liquor, army at Miss World pageant.

text.p: India's Supreme Court ruled on Friday that the organisers of the Miss World beauty pageant could serve liquor at the event and deploy soldiers to prevent threatened attacks.
A three-judge bench rejected a lower court ruling that had barred Amitabh Bachchan Corp Ltd (ABCL) from offering liquor during Saturday's pageant in the southern city of Bangalore.

The Karnataka state High Court ruled on Tuesday that the controversial pageant, dogged by protests and threats of attack, could go ahead, but said the state could not deploy either the army or Border Security Force (BSF) paramilitary units.
More than 10,000 security officers were expected to patrol the streets and stadium on Saturday.
Following the Karanataka High Court order, authorities were planning to rely on police and troopers from paramilitary forces other than the BSF.

ABCL submitted an affidavit to the Supreme Court on Friday promising to serve liquor to selected guests only at the beginning and end of the pageant. It also said it would pay for the security expenses.
Bangalore police said on Friday they would begin detaining militant activists ahead of the pageant, which has provoked threats of multiple suicide protests.
Police were tailing Kinay Narayana Shashikala, leader of a traditionalist women's group whose members said they would burn themselves alive if the show went ahead on Saturday.
A group calling itself the Indian Tigers has said 400 activists would infiltrate the crowd and carry out lightning attacks inside and outside the stadium where the event was set to be held.
